eventMetadata.context_description:
**High pressure building across southern England is driving trader consensus toward a peak of 32–33°C in London on July 29, with Met Office guidance indicating a maximum of 33°C under mostly sunny skies and light winds.** 

Recent model runs show warm southerly flow advecting air from the continent, supporting daytime highs several degrees above the July average of ~22–24°C, consistent with the ongoing warm spell across southeast England. Minor forecast spread arises from differences in predicted cloud cover timing, boundary-layer mixing, and the strength of the urban heat-island effect in central London, which can add 1–2°C locally. Official agencies such as the Met Office and ECMWF continue to converge on dry, stable conditions with little risk of significant cooling until later in the week, leaving the outcome sensitive to the final 24–48 hours of model updates. Traders therefore assign the highest implied probabilities to the narrow 32–34°C band while assigning low odds to extremes below 30°C or above 35°C.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent European heatwave conditions, driven by a persistent high-pressure system and warm air advection from southern regions, position Paris for a likely daily maximum near 37–38°C on July 29. Ensemble forecasts from major models show tight clustering around these values due to minimal expected cloud cover and light winds, which maximize daytime solar heating while limiting mixing with cooler air aloft. Urban heat island effects in central Paris further elevate observed readings by 1–2°C relative to rural stations. Short-range model runs through July 27 indicate low probability of significant cooling fronts or convective clouds that could cap temperatures below 36°C or push them to 39°C+, though minor shifts in boundary-layer moisture could still differentiate the top outcomes. Updated Météo-France guidance and next model cycles will refine these thresholds ahead of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Wellington’s winter climate features average July daily maxima near 12–13°C, with highs rarely exceeding 15°C or dropping below 10°C amid frequent southerly winds and frontal passages. Current numerical weather prediction models from MetService and international ensembles converge on a 12–14°C range for July 29, driven by a transient ridge delivering mostly fine conditions before increasing cloud and a possible weak front, with light northerly flow limiting daytime warming. The recent July 22 high of exactly 14°C illustrates how quickly model consensus can shift probabilities, and NIWA’s seasonal outlook for near- or below-average temperatures reinforces the modest upside risk. Traders therefore assign the highest implied probabilities to 13°C and 14°C, reflecting tight forecast spreads and typical day-to-day variability in the capital’s exposed coastal setting two days before resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Dallas Love Field Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 29 Jul '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Dallas Love Field Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/us/tx/dallas/KDAL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service and AccuWeather guidance points to mostly sunny conditions under a strong high-pressure ridge for Dallas on July 29, with afternoon highs likely peaking in the 100–104°F range amid typical late-July southerly flow and dew points near 70°F. Model consensus shows limited spread, driven by minimal moisture return and no significant frontal passage, though small timing differences in any scattered high clouds could trim peak readings by 1–2°F. Historical July climatology for DFW supports upper-90s to low-100s as the norm, with the market’s tight clustering around 98–103°F reflecting traders’ assessment of these stable atmospheric conditions and the narrow window for last-minute forecast adjustments before official NWS verification.
